messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High 5xx rate observed for frontend ELB (us-west-2a). Alert source: ELB-health-checks. routing_key=sre-oncall

sre-oncall: seeing ~35% 502/504 at the edge for a couple minutes. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/xyz/elbs?orgId=1 (:rotating_light:)

sanjay: confirmed spike in p95 latency and connection resets targeting elb-prod-usw2a. Affected target group tg-prod-frontend-usw2a.

sre-oncall: @nora can you take primary? I'm already on a different pager.

nora: taking it. reassigning PD. On it. quick check: any recent deploys?

sanjay: no deploys in the last 30m. Metrics show backend EC2s healthy, but ELB target unhealthy counts rising and new connections failing TLS handshake sometimes.

kevin: looks like Route53 failsafe routing didn't kick — weights still 100% to us-west-2. TTL is 300s. Suggest lowering to 60 and shift weight while we investigate.

nora: do that. I'll open an AWS support case too.

(elaine reacted :thumbsup:)

aws-support-bot: Support case opened: 1234567890 — Engineer assigned. ETA initial response 15m.

nora: changing Route53 record from weight=100 us-west-2 -> weight=50 us-west-2, weight=50 us-east-1. Lowering TTL to 60. Pushing now.

kevin: running CLI to change record:
```bash
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z111AAA --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"app.redwood.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-east-1","Weight":50,"AliasTarget":{"HostedZoneId":"Z222","DNSName":"dualstack-elb-east-1.amazonaws.com.","EvaluateTargetHealth":false}}]}'
```

kevin: TTL lowered -> 60s. Waiting for propagation.

nora: meanwhile draining unhealthy targets in tg-prod-frontend-usw2a to force new connections to healthy AZs:
```bash
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --targets Id=i-0abcd1234
```

sre-oncall: note: draining may cause brief 503s for existing connections but should stop fresh failures. Proceeding.

sanjay: rolling IP-level autoscaling up in us-west-2: add 4 instances in other AZs and attach to target group as hot spares.

(incident-bot: +1 oncall handover)

oncall-manager: nora take full ownership; if route53 shift doesn't reduce errors in 5m, escalate to runbook: cross-region-failover and notify sales & status page.

nora: ack. status page draft: "We are investigating increased error rates in us-west-2 impacting some customers. Traffic is being shifted to alternate region and mitigations in progress." Posting now.

kevin: early telemetry: error rate dropped to ~12% after route53 changes and TTL effect kicking in. p95 latency improving.

aws-support-bot: AWS has detected elevated networking errors affecting ELB control plane in us-west-2a; engineers investigating. Suggested mitigation: shift traffic out of the affected AZ and avoid new capacity provisioning in that AZ.

nora: copying recommended mitigation: we won't provision new instances in us-west-2a and will prefer us-west-2b/c and us-east-1. Updating autoscaling groups to exclude AZ 'a'.

(elaine: adding note to incident timeline)

sanjay: customer impact: partial traffic loss for customers pinned to us-west-2a; some backend requests returning 502/504. CS has been notified and will triage high-impact accounts.

nora: oncall handoff at 30m mark -> I'm handing to kevin for next shift. kevin you'll take primary after me at +30.

kevin: taking over. I'll keep watch on Route53 weights and ELB unhealthy count. If error rate <5% for 15m, start controlled rollback of DNS weights to original gradually.

oncall-manager: good timeline. keep logs of actions for postmortem. We'll run blameless RCA once incident steadied.

nora: summary for post: cause suspected ELB control plane networking issues in us-west-2a causing TLS handshake failures and target registration flaps. Mitigations: (1) Route53 weighted shift to other regions, TTL lowered, (2) drain targets in affected AZ, (3) avoid provisioning in AZ a, (4) scale out healthy AZs, (5) opened AWS support case. Next: add permanent runbook step to automatically decrease weights when ELB health threshold exceeded.

kevin: status update 20m later: error rate now ~2.1%, p95 back to normal. Leaving monitoring on. Marking as mitigated but still investigatory.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: Mitigated — monitoring. Severity: SEV2. Case 1234567890 open with AWS.

nora: thanks all, handing over to kevin. please update oncall calendar and incident doc. Will create postmortem ticket.

(elaine reacted :party:)
